question: Why does gold tend to do well when real interest rates are low?
baseline_top3: Gold pays no interest or dividend, so when real rates are high, holding gold has a high opportunity cost and its price tends to face pressure. When real rates are low or negative, that cost shrinks and gold often does well.
Central bank purchases, inflation expectations, and geopolitical uncertainty also play important roles in gold price formation.
The US dollar and gold have historically moved in opposite directions; a weaker dollar makes gold cheaper for foreign buyers.
reranked_top3: Gold pays no interest or dividend, so when real rates are high, holding gold has a high opportunity cost and its price tends to face pressure. When real rates are low or negative, that cost shrinks and gold often does well.
TIPS yields (Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities) are a common proxy for US real rates and are often cited in gold market commentary.
Inflation expectations embedded in breakeven rates influence the gold price because gold is widely held as an inflation hedge.
